provenance.method: lesson notes written from the NERDC 2025 scheme of work outline; every week keeps its scheme topic and bullets as the teaching spine

topics.title: Count 51 to 70
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to count numbers 51 to 70.
The pupils should be able to write numbers 51 to 70.

Introduction:
We can count up to 50. Today we will count higher.
Let us learn numbers 51 to 70.

Content:
Count in tens 50, 60, 70.
Count one by one 51, 52, 53...70.
Write the numbers on the board.
Point to number 55. What comes after?

Class activity:
Number line walk. Draw numbers on floor.
Pupils jump and count from 51 to 70.

Evaluation questions:
Count from 60 to 70.
Write number 65.
What comes after 59?

Summary:
We can count and write numbers 51 to 70.

topics.title: Count 71 to 90
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to count numbers 71 to 90.
The pupils should be able to write numbers 71 to 90.

Introduction:
We counted up to 70 last week.
Today we will count to 90.

Content:
Count in tens 70, 80, 90.
Count one by one 71, 72, 73...90.
Write the numbers on the board.
Show number 85. What comes before?

Class activity:
Number line walk. Draw numbers on floor.
Pupils walk and count from 71 to 90.

Evaluation questions:
Count from 80 to 90.
Write number 75.
What comes after 79?

Summary:
We can count and write numbers 71 to 90.

topics.title: Count 91 to 100
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to count numbers 91 to 100.
The pupils should be able to write numbers 91 to 100.

Introduction:
We almost reach 100.
Today we count the last numbers.

Content:
Count in tens 90, 100.
Count one by one 91, 92, 93...100.
Write the numbers on the board.
Show number 99. What comes next?

Class activity:
We reached 100 party. Pupils clap and count to 100.
Each pupil says one number.

Evaluation questions:
Count from 95 to 100.
Write number 98.
What comes after 99?

Summary:
We can count and write numbers 91 to 100.

topics.title: Counting 1 to 100
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to count from 1 to 100.
The pupils should be able to fill a hundred chart.

Introduction:
We learned numbers 1 to 100.
Today we practice counting all together.

Content:
Count by tens 10, 20, 30...100.
Count all numbers 1 to 100.
Fill the missing numbers on a chart.
Point to number 42. What is before and after?

Class activity:
Fill the hundred chart. Pupils write missing numbers.
Count in groups of ten.

Evaluation questions:
Count from 1 to 100.
Fill number 55 on the chart.
What comes after 29?

Summary:
We can count from 1 to 100.

topics.title: Adding with objects
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to add two groups of objects.
The pupils should be able to write the sum.

Introduction:
We can count objects.
Today we add two groups together.

Content:
Add two groups of counters.
Example: 2 apples + 3 apples = 5 apples.
Count all objects together.
Write the sum 2 + 3 = 5.

Class activity:
Pupils get counters and add in pairs.
One pupil puts 2 counters, other puts 3.
Count total together.

Evaluation questions:
Add 4 + 2.
Add 3 + 3.
What is 5 + 1?

Summary:
We can add two groups of objects.

topics.title: Adding small numbers
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to add small numbers.
The pupils should be able to draw and add.

Introduction:
We learned adding with objects.
Today we add without objects.

Content:
2 plus 1 is 3.
3 plus 2 is 5.
Draw pictures to show adding.
Example: draw 2 circles, add 1 more.

Class activity:
Pupils draw pictures and add.
Draw 4 stars, add 2 more stars.
Count total stars.

Evaluation questions:
What is 2 + 2?
What is 3 + 1?
Draw 3 + 4.

Summary:
We can add small numbers.

topics.title: Taking away
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to take away with counters.
The pupils should be able to write what is left.

Introduction:
We learned adding.
Today we take away objects.

Content:
Take away with counters.
Example: 5 balls, take away 2 balls.
Count what is left.
Write 5 - 2 = 3.

Class activity:
Pupils get 5 counters.
Take away 2 counters.
Count what is left.

Evaluation questions:
What is 4 - 1?
What is 6 - 3?
Take away 2 from 5.

Summary:
We can take away objects.

topics.title: Number before and after
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to find number before and after.
The pupils should be able to fill before and after.

Introduction:
Numbers have neighbors.
Today we find number neighbors.

Content:
What comes before 8? 7.
What comes after 8? 9.
Number before is one less.
Number after is one more.

Class activity:
Fill before and after.
Pupils hold number cards.
Find who comes before and after.

Evaluation questions:
What comes before 5?
What comes after 7?
Fill before and after for 10.

Summary:
We can find number neighbors.

topics.title: Comparing numbers
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to compare big and small numbers.
The pupils should be able to use more than and less than.

Introduction:
Some numbers are bigger.
Some numbers are smaller.

Content:
Bigger and smaller numbers.
Example: 8 is bigger than 5.
Use more than, less than.
5 is less than 8.

Class activity:
Use objects to compare.
Pupils compare groups of counters.
Say which is more or less.

Evaluation questions:
Which is bigger, 7 or 9?
Which is less, 4 or 6?
Use more than to compare 3 and 5.

Summary:
We can compare numbers.

topics.title: Revision and maths fair
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to add numbers.
The pupils should be able to take away numbers.

Introduction:
We learned many things.
Today we play maths games.

Content:
Add and take away relay.
Number chart race.
Count from 1 to 100.
Find number neighbors.

Class activity:
Add and take away relay.
Pupils run to board to solve problems.
Number chart race.
Fill missing numbers quickly.

Evaluation questions:
What is 2 + 3?
What is 5 - 1?
Count from 70 to 80.

Summary:
We had fun with maths games.
